# Reader contract fixtures

These small files are read by the Rust and JavaScript test suites. Overviews
use the `quantized_geoarrow` encoding.

## Generated by the Rust tests

`refinement`, `shared`, `distinct-boundaries` and `renamed-overview` come from
the Rust integration test `shared_lod_contract_fixtures`. They contain two
LineStrings with IDs 0 and 1. ID 0 enters at resolution 8; ID 1 enters at
resolution 1. Coordinates are deliberately chosen so quantization changes the
overview bounds. The producer writes MultiLineString overviews.

- `refinement.parquet`: producer output with bbox PageIndexes. The final two
  levels share a row-group boundary and use different LoDs. Overview integers
  use `DELTA_BINARY_PACKED` with ZSTD compression.
- `shared.parquet`: an additional resolution-4 level referencing `l1` on RG 0;
  resolution 1 also references `l1` through RG 1. No bbox ColumnIndexes.
- `distinct-boundaries.parquet`: each level has its own row-group boundary,
  without bbox ColumnIndexes. This and `shared.parquet` rewrite only the metadata
  and use the Parquet writer's default encodings, independent of the producer's
  encoding policy.
- `renamed-overview.parquet`: `refinement.parquet` with its overview column
  renamed to `render_geometry`, recorded in `geo.lod.overviews.column`.

`base-covering.parquet` and `base-no-covering.parquet` have no overviews. They
exercise ordinary attributes named `overviews`, independent bbox roots, and
missing statistics/covering.

`attribute-encodings.parquet` covers dictionary-free `PLAIN` attribute encoding
and `DELTA_BINARY_PACKED` overview integers with ZSTD compression, including
nested nullable values, integer extremes, floats, strings, and binary. Rust
verifies all original values after conversion; JS checks decoding of the same
fixture.

Normal test runs write only to temporary directories. Regenerate these files
explicitly from the repository root:

```sh
COGP_TEST_FIXTURE_DIR="$PWD/test-data" cargo test -p cogp --test end_to_end
```

## Generated by Python

`quantized-geoarrow-linestring.parquet`, `quantized-geoarrow-multilinestring.parquet`,
`quantized-geoarrow-polygon.parquet` and `quantized-geoarrow-multipolygon.parquet`
cover each `quantized_geoarrow` geometry type, including holes, multipart
geometries, and a LoD shared by two levels. Their overview column is named
`render_geometry`, next to an ordinary attribute named `overviews`. The overview
coordinates test the decoding transform and do not match the primary geometry.
Regenerate them with pyarrow installed:

```sh
python3 cogp-js/test/fixtures/generate-quantized-geoarrow.py
```
